text:
I

My little box
from Olinalá,
rosewood,
jacaranda.

When I open it
it suddenly gives
its scent, fit for
the Queen of Sheba.

Ah, what a breath,
tropical: clove,
mahogany
and copal!

I set it here,
I leave it there;
along the corridors
it comes and goes.

It boils with patterns
like a country:
nopal, deer,
quail,

volcanoes
with towering necks,
and the Indian, airy
as the corn.

This is how they paint it,
just so, just so,
with Indian fingers
or hummingbird's;

and this is how
a masterful
Aztec hand makes it,
a quetzal hand.

II

When night
is drawing near,
so it may guard me
from its harm,

I place it
beneath my head,
where others put
their treasure.

Lovely dreams
it makes me dream;
it makes me laugh,
it makes me weep:

hand in hand
we cross the sea,
twin mountain ranges,
fields to plow.

Anáhuac
shines bright;
the beast Ajusco
is poised to leap,

and by the road
that leads toward the sea,
one goes to meet
Quetzalcoatl.

She is my breath,
I am her walk;
she is knowledge,
I am delirium.

And we stop,
like manna,
where the road
ends in abundance,

where the women
of Olinalá
shout to us: “Halalá!”
